newsitem.title: USA: Prosecutors, defense spar over Oklahoma bomb papers.
newsitem.headline: Prosecutors, defense spar over Oklahoma bomb papers.

text.p: Prosecutors in the Oklahoma City bombing case on Wednesday said they had given volumes of evidence to the defence, which claimed that documents were handed over too slowly and were poorly organised.

Prosecutor Beth Wilkinson told the judge in the first day of a three-day pre-trial hearing that government lawyers have handed over 25,000 witness statements, 477 laboratory reports and 30,000 photographs to defence attorneys.
Timothy McVeigh and Terry Nichols are charged in the bombing of the Alfred P. Murrah federal building that killed 168 people. Both defendants were in the courtroom.

But Stephen Jones, McVeigh's attorney, said the index of the information was so disorganized it was a "mishmash," making it difficult for the defence to identify the evidence properly and prepare for trial.

Jones said defence lawyers were being "showered with paper" when the evidence was not critical. But in sensitive issues the "papers get vague." Some requests were made 500 days ago, not long after the bombing, Jones said.

Jones reserved some of his toughest criticism for the FBI's forensic laboratory and said he wanted to know if agents had been criticised before for the way they conducted tests similar to ones in the bombing case.
But Jones also said he believed the hearing was useful. "I think the logjam is breaking up and we're going to get what we need to defend our client," Jones told reporters.
Jones said the defence intended to challenge every aspect of the government's case. He said there could be a "John Doe" No. 2, 3, 4, or even 5 responsible for the bombing.
Prosecutors are obliged to provide defence lawyers evidence they will or might use in a trial. They must also hand over any information that might help the defence side.
At one point, the judge told a prosecutor to hand over to the defence a data base compiled of telephone company records. "You provide the data base. That's an order," Matsch snapped.
The defendants will be tried separately. McVeigh will be tried first and his case is expected to begin sometime next year.
